transcript:
Header: 2025-07-22 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~46 mins | Recording: Fireflies.ai export
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood ML), Sofia Lopez (AstraMetrics ML Lead), Ben Yoon (AstraMetrics SRE), Rina Patel (AstraMetrics PM)

00:00 Maya Chen: okay, hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off the quant ablation sync. quick agenda: results, tune ideas, and go/no-go for the small canary.
00:12 Sofia Lopez: sounds good. we've been watching the accuracy dips on the QA slices, that's our primary blocker.
00:20 Daniel Ruiz: right, so we ran three ablations: uniform INT8 across all layers, per-layer INT8 with selective fp16 for top-k layers, and hybrid FP8 fallback for the answer-generation head. i'll summarize numbers first.
00:35 Daniel Ruiz: on the retrieval+QA suite (3.2k queries) exact-match baseline fp16 was 79.4%. uniform INT8 dropped to 73.1% (delta -6.3), per-layer INT8 recovered to 76.8 (delta -2.6), and hybrid FP8 kept us at 78.9 (~-0.5). so hybrid looks promising for QA.
01:02 Ben Yoon: those are big deltas for production. what's the latency impact?
01:08 Daniel Ruiz: p50 token latency: fp16 avg 28ms, uniform INT8 22ms, per-layer INT8 23ms, hybrid FP8 24ms. p90: fp16 68ms, int8 54ms, hybrid 57ms. throughput wise tokens/sec improved ~26% uniformly for INT8.
01:30 Rina Patel: and memory? we're constrained to 16GB GPUs in our private cluster.
01:35 Daniel Ruiz: uniform INT8 reduced peak memory by ~38%, per-layer depends on which layers kept fp16 — our per-layer config used fp16 on first 4 layers which kept memory at about -30% vs fp16. hybrid FP8 landed at -33% memory.
01:55 Priya Nair: quick note, the per-layer strategy helps since the early attention layers are sensitivity hotspots, we saw lower KL divergence when preserving fp16 there.
02:12 Sofia Lopez: can you explain the calibration process? we saw a weird regression on long-context summarization.
02:19 Daniel Ruiz: yeah so calibration seed and clipped quant ranges matter. we used usual min-max per-block, then a per-channel adjustment using 2000 calibration tokens. for summarization, FP8 showed variance in ROUGE-L on long docs — about -3 points for uniform INT8, per-layer was -1.1 and hybrid FP8 -0.6. it's likely due to KV-cache scaling and attention softmax numerical shifts.
02:50 Ben Yoon: are these numbers from a single run? how noisy are they?
02:54 Daniel Ruiz: these are means over 3 seeds, SD about 0.7% for QA EM and 0.9 ROUGE points. we should run larger eval to stabilize.
03:10 Maya Chen: okay so hybrids look like the best tradeoff for AstraMetrics' QA workloads. question for Sofia: what SLOs would be acceptable for a canary?
03:20 Sofia Lopez: we can't accept >2% absolute drop on QA exact-match across critical intents; latency p90 must stay under 80ms for single-turn inference.
03:30 Maya Chen: noted. hybrid FP8 seems within that envelope based on current numbers.
03:36 Rina Patel: what about tail failure modes — hallucination or answer truncation?
03:42 Daniel Ruiz: we instrumented answer-coverage and hallucination score (heuristic). hallucination rate increased from 1.8% to 2.3% on uniform INT8, per-layer to 2.0%, hybrid 1.9%. not great but within our rollback thresholds.
04:05 Sofia Lopez: can you show example failures?
04:08 Daniel Ruiz: yes, i've dropped two typical QA fails into the shared doc — one is numerical precision on dates, another is truncated context when KV cache scaled down.
04:20 Maya Chen: action item: SE to share the failing prompt list and per-case diff.
04:25 Daniel Ruiz: done, will post after call.
04:30 Priya Nair: a tuning knob we tried was block-wise mixed precision: quantize middle blocks aggressively and keep first/last 3 layers at fp16. that reduced QA delta to -1.4 and kept memory at -28%. it's more deterministic than purely per-layer heuristics.
04:58 Ben Yoon: how much more complex is that to implement in our runtime? we have custom runtime constraints on pre/post processing.
05:07 Daniel Ruiz: Redwood runtime supports block-level configs via the model profile. we can export a profile JSON; it's a one-line flag at load time to apply the block quant schema. some runtime restarts needed for a canary.
05:24 Sofia Lopez: cost-wise, what's the delta if we go hybrid FP8 in hosted vs our dedicated private?
05:30 Maya Chen: rough schtick: tokens cost drops ~25% with INT8/hybrid on hosted; on Dedicated the savings translate to headcount and capacity needed — estimated 18-22% infra cost saving. we'll send a detailed cost model.
05:45 Rina Patel: do we need to worry about SOC2 or encryption with calibration scripts?
05:50 Maya Chen: calibration runs can be done in-customer VPC; we can also provide encrypted artifact storage. Redwood supports KMS integrations and audit logs.
06:02 Sofia Lopez: great. for canary planning, we want a staged rollout: 1% traffic -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback on quality regressions. can Redwood support that?
06:14 Daniel Ruiz: yes, rollout policies support percent-based routing and automated metric checks. we can set threshold alarms on QA EM and hallucination heuristics.
06:25 Maya Chen: propose timeline: get extended 12k eval next week, then synthetic canary for 1% production shadowing 48 hours, then 5% with active traffic if metrics stable.
06:36 Sofia Lopez: sounds good. two asks: (1) show per-layer calibration script and its runtime overhead, (2) add the long-doc summarization test into the extended eval.
06:48 Daniel Ruiz: will do both.
06:52 Ben Yoon: small question: any IP/obligation on the calibration code?
06:56 Maya Chen: we generally provide the script under permissive SOW for pilots; for production we'll nail licensing in the contract.
07:05 Rina Patel: ok that's fine.
07:08 Maya Chen: any other questions?
07:10 Sofia Lopez: nothing else from me.
07:12 Maya Chen: cool. quick recap and owners — see action items. we'll aim to share the extended eval results on 7/29. thanks everyone.
07:25 End of recording

Notes: transcription contains a few mis-heard acronyms (K-V cache transcribed as K V cache), filler words retained, and occasional speaker IDs are approximate.
